outcome: No proof, disproof, new large NSW prime discovery, or any other development bearing on the infinitude of Newman–Shanks–Williams primes was found since 26 January 2024; the question remains an open conjecture with no recorded change in the window.
summary: Newman–Shanks–Williams (NSW) primes are primes of the form ((1+√2)^n + (1-√2)^n)/2 for odd n, equivalently half of certain companion Pell numbers; the known terms correspond to OEIS A088165, with indices 3, 5, 7, 19, 29, 47, 59, 163 (and a 99-digit ninth term too large for the OEIS b-file entry). The largest known genuine (proven) NSW prime, for n = 9679 (3705 digits), was found in 2001, and the largest known NSW probable prime, for n = 172243 (65931 digits), was found in 2007 — both well before the frozen revision date, and no source found reports any new NSW prime, probable prime, or record extension since then, let alone since January 2024. I checked the OEIS entry A088165 for new terms or comments (none post-2008), the Wikipedia article on NSW primes (no dates past 2007 given, no mention of the infinitude question being addressed), t5k.org's 'largest known prime by year' history (no mention of NSW primes at all, largest-prime records dominated by Mersenne primes), and general web searches for any 2024/2025 NSW prime discovery, PrimeGrid announcements, or a proof/disproof of infinitude — all came up empty. This mirrors the closely related open questions for Fibonacci primes, Mersenne primes, and other primes-in-a-linear-recurrence sequences, none of which have been resolved either. No AI system appears anywhere in connection with this problem in the window. This is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' record: the infinitude question is exactly the kind of existence question (§3.1) that is not advanced by finding another term or extending a search bound, and no such extension was even found to have occurred.
competing_reading: None found — no candidate event exists to argue about a different classification for. If an unreported PrimeGrid or GIMPS-adjacent project has found a new NSW prime or probable prime since 2007, it did not surface in searches or on the relevant OEIS/Wikipedia/t5k.org pages, which are the natural places such a record would be logged.
what_would_settle_it: A new entry in OEIS A088165 (or its b-file) with a post-January-2024 date, a PrimeGrid or similar distributed-computing project announcement of a new NSW prime/probable prime, an update to the NSW prime Wikipedia article's 'largest known' figures, or a paper addressing the infinitude of primes represented by the Pell/NSW recurrence.
